name: Technical Writing Conventions
description: This module defines the naming, formatting, and structural style conventions to follow whenever writing, implementing, or reviewing technical writing code or output, so results stay consistent with the existing technical writing style guide.
content:
This module defines the naming, formatting, and structural style conventions to follow whenever writing, implementing, or reviewing technical writing code or output, so results stay consistent with the existing technical writing style guide.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Before starting technical writing work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
2. Measure before optimizing any technical writing bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
3. Surface known limitations of a chosen technical writing approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
4. Keep technical writing outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
5. Re-check edge cases relevant to technical writing (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
6. Keep technical writing changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
7. When multiple technical writing strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
8. Check that technical writing terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
9. Prefer explicit, readable technical writing solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
10. Prefer the simplest technical writing approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
11. Validate technical writing outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not silently drop technical writing edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not apply generic technical writing advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of technical writing correctness.
- Avoid mixing unrelated technical writing concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these technical writing guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
